name: Old PTU
note: The old Navy PT uniform, the blue sweats issued at recruit training. Sailors called it the smurfs. This is the first uniform in the record.

name: New PTU
note: The newer Navy physical training uniform.

name: EODMU 5 PT
context: Command PT gear, EOD Mobile Unit Five
note: Command physical training gear from EOD Mobile Unit Five.

name: JCSE PT
context: Command PT gear, Joint Communications Support Element
note: Command physical training gear from the Joint Communications Support Element.

name: EODMU 5
context: Organizational clothing, EOD Mobile Unit Five
note: EOD Mobile Unit Five organizational clothing: the tan shirt worn with olive cargo diver shorts.

name: JCSE (AFG)
context: Civilian attire, Afghanistan, Joint Communications Support Element
note: Civilian attire worn in Afghanistan with JCSE: a red polo, 5.11 cargo pants, and tan boots.

name: Dungarees
note: Blue denim trousers and a chambray shirt, the ordinary working uniform before the blue digital camouflage.

name: Utilities
note: Listed in the record as its own uniform, separate from dungarees and from the later camouflage. Which utility pattern is not further described.

name: Coveralls
note: One-piece shipboard coveralls, the practical uniform for work in a machinery space or on deck. Associated with sea duty.

name: Summer Whites
note: A white working uniform for hot climates, simpler than dress whites.

name: Winter Blues
note: The black winter working uniform, nicknamed the Johnny Cash because it was black shirt and black trousers.

name: NWU Type I
note: The Navy's blue digital working uniform, the Type I, often called blueberries.

name: NWU Type III
note: The Navy’s green digital working uniform, the Type III.

name: Peanut Butters
context: Navy Service Uniform, E-6 and below
note: The Navy Service Uniform that replaced the winter blues (the Johnny Cash) and the summer whites. Sailors called it peanut butters for the khaki shirt. Black trousers and a black garrison cap went with it. Worn until he made chief. A chief's khaki has khaki trousers, not these black ones.

name: E7 Whites
note: The chief’s summer white uniform.

name: E7 Khakis
note: Making chief replaces the jumper uniforms with chief's uniforms: service khaki, dress blue, and dress white among them. The record says nearly all of them were worn, and dinner dress was not.

name: Summer Whites
note: The white jumper, the crackerjack, worn for inspections and ceremonies in summer whites season. The chief's version is a different coat.

name: Winter Blues
note: The Navy dress blue jumper, the crackerjack, with the broad collar and white piping, for sailors below chief. The chief's dress blue is a coat, not this jumper.

name: E7 Dress Whites
note: The chief’s dress white uniform.

name: E7 Dress Blues
note: The chief’s dress blue coat. The photograph in this case is this uniform.

name: Woodland BDU
note: The woodland-pattern Battle Dress Uniform. The Navy Working Uniform Type III, the other green pattern, is shown with the work uniforms.

name: Desert DCU
note: Desert camouflage worn with the Iraq tours. The exact pattern, often the three-color desert uniform in that era, is not confirmed.

name: ACU (Army)
note: The Army Combat Uniform in the gray-green digital pattern, worn for the individual-augmentee tour. The record called it the Army AWU.

name: Multicam (Army)
note: The Army's Multicam (Operational Camouflage Pattern) uniform, worn with the joint communications deployments to Afghanistan.
